sample_data.method: The Next.js fallback imports Data/P11_route_shift_public.json directly, and the Spring DataSeeder loads the same published fixture into an empty PostgreSQL database.
sample_data.reset_instructions: Browser mode: remove routeboard-workspace-v1 from localStorage and reload. Backend mode: use an empty PostgreSQL database and restart the API; OPTIMIZER_SEED_CASE_ID selects the case and defaults to PUB-01.

problem_solving_method: Built a deterministic route and shift planner around one reusable hard-rule validator. Jobs are ordered by time-window urgency, evaluated at every route insertion position, and assigned by minimum added travel with window risk as a tiebreaker. A local-search pass attempts feasible relocations and swaps to reduce total travel. Every unscheduled job receives a specific blocking reason, and the same validation rules protect manual reassignment and active replanning.

team_members.major_contribution: Frontend application, in-browser planner, backend integration, persistence workflows, UI and analytics, public-data seeding integration, deployment configuration, testing, and documentation.
Initial Spring Boot backend, data models, controllers, assignment and local-search services, persistence layer, and backend test suite.

major_design_decisions: One validator for every scheduling path: automatic assignment, manual moves, emergency replanning, and sick-day redistribution share the same hard-rule checks.
Deterministic greedy insertion plus bounded local search: the planner stays explainable and fast for the published problem size without adding a heavyweight solver.

Server-side API proxy with a browser fallback: deployed Next.js routes use the standalone Spring API, while the published fixtures and TypeScript planner keep the evaluation workflow usable when the backend is unavailable.
Operational UI without chart or drag-and-drop dependencies: CSS timelines and analytical bars plus native drag events keep the interface compact and the dependency surface small.
known_limitations: The live Spring API operates on one active dataset case at a time; selecting another seed case requires an empty database and OPTIMIZER_SEED_CASE_ID before startup.
The application has no authentication or multi-tenant access control; it is designed as a single-team event prototype.
Native HTML drag-and-drop is optimized for pointer devices and does not provide a dedicated touch reordering interaction.
